etymologies.etymologyHTML: From social +‎ -ize.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To interact with others, especially personally, informally and off the clock rather than formally and officially.

quote.citation: 2006, Christopher Duncan, “Managing Your Management”, in Dominic Shakeshaft, editor, The Career Programmer: Guerilla Tactics for an Imperfect World (The Expert’s Voice), 2nd edition, Berkeley, Calif.: Apress, →ISBN, part II (Guerilla Tactics for Front-line Programmers), page 171:
quote.text: When socializing it's important that you never talk business unless they bring it up. If you do, you'll find out quickly that you're no longer invited to any of the really good reindeer games. Rather, be a good listener.
The UU is a great place to be on campus to socialize but when business needs to be taken care of the five story library is the place to be!

quote.citation: 2024 November 15, Julie Lasky, “A Glass Addition Maximizes Light and Minimizes Exposure”, in The New York Times‎[1]:
quote.text: Mr. Bach is an architect who, with his wife and professional partner, Anna Bach, regularly socializes with Ms. Aguirre and Mr. Ferrer.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To instruct (somebody), usually subconsciously and mostly by example, in the etiquette of a society.

quote.citation: 1977, Dorothy Rogers, Issues in child psychology, page 62:
quote.text: That is, by way of this initial imprinting the young animal becomes a socialized member of its species. Animals misimprinted to other species show a variety of abnormal social behaviors as adults.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To take something into collective or governmental ownership.
